criteria.criterion: A new skill markdown file exists in a skills directory (e.g. skills/diagnose-failure.md) giving ordered steps: read the stored failures and check tails, state the cause as something other than a restatement of the event, compare with earlier cases, name the evidence cited, and say what to do when evidence is missing.
criteria.evidence: I read crates/athena-context/skills/diagnose-failure.md in the diff. It is titled 'version 1' and has 7 ordered steps: (1) read the stored failures and the tail of each failed check's output, (3) state the cause as something other than a restatement of the event, (4) compare with earlier cases, (5) name the evidence, (6) say what to do when evidence is missing. It sits in a skills directory, though not at the example path.

criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-context or crates/athena-core builds the introspection brief and asserts it contains the skill text; run `cargo test` and it passes.
criteria.evidence: The new test the_introspection_of_a_rejected_job_is_given_the_diagnose_failure_skill runs a rejected job through the fake model and records the system prompt it receives. It then asserts the prompt contains the trimmed skill file. I ran it and it passed (1 passed). The test is in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs, not athena-context or athena-core, but that file is on the deliverables list. Before the change the system prompt was SYSTEM_PROMPT alone, so this test would have failed. The full suite passed in CI (recorded check).

criteria.criterion: `cargo test` passes and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded fmt check failed. I reran `cargo fmt --all --check` and it exits 1: introspect.rs line 1029, `pub const DIAGNOSE_FAILURE_SKILL: &str = include_str!(...)`, is too long and rustfmt wants it split over two lines. Clippy and tests passed in CI (recorded checks).

criteria.criterion: The skill file contains no secrets or personal data and no system-specific instructions outside clearly labeled examples; it is written for an outside reader.
criteria.evidence: I read the skill text. It contains no secrets, emails or names. The steps are generic: stored failures, checks, cases, evidence. The one concrete scenario is marked 'Example (labeled, for illustration only)'. The prose is plain and needs no prior knowledge of the system.

criteria.criterion: No existing prompt set exceeds its token budget; reader and verifier prompt files are untouched.
criteria.evidence: The diff touches no file under crates/athena-context/prompts/. The skill is added to introspect.rs's own SYSTEM_PROMPT string, which is not part of the budgeted role sets in athena-context/src/lib.rs. So no budgeted set changes, and the CI test run, which includes the budget tests, passed.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the skill and the outcome: introspection of a failed job now follows the stated method.
criteria.evidence: Under Added, the new CHANGELOG.md entry names the `diagnose-failure` skill (version 1) and its path. It says 'The introspection of a failed job now follows the stated method' because the skill text is part of the system prompt.

findings.summary: cargo fmt --check fails on the new constant
findings.evidence: `cargo fmt --all --check` exits 1. rustfmt wants `pub const DIAGNOSE_FAILURE_SKILL: &str =` split from the `include_str!(...)` on the next line. The recorded CI fmt check also failed. This violates criterion 3 and the 'tested' default.

findings.summary: The skill file is at a path outside the deliverables list
findings.evidence: The list expects skills/diagnose-failure.md, but the change creates crates/athena-context/skills/diagnose-failure.md. Keeping it inside a crate makes sense, because include_str! needs a path that survives packaging. Still, it is a file outside the stated scope. briefs.rs is on the list but unchanged, which is fine: it is not needed.

findings.summary: The skill bypasses the existing versioned, hashed prompt-asset mechanism, so a record cannot show which method version was used
findings.evidence: athena-context/src/lib.rs already defines PromptAsset {id, version, text}, whose hashes are recorded as context components. The skill is instead pasted into a format! string, and its version exists only in the markdown heading. The request's complaint was 'who knows what the method was like'. Registering the skill as a PromptAsset, or recording its sha256 in the introspection record, would make the method traceable per job.

summary: This change fails because `cargo fmt --check` is not clean. Otherwise it does what was asked: it adds a short skill file (version 1) with a stepwise method for diagnosing a failed job, and puts that method into the introspection's system prompt. A new test checks that the prompt the model receives contains the full skill text; I ran it and it passed. The CHANGELOG entry describes the change correctly, no prompt files or token budgets are touched, and the skill is generic, with its one example labeled. The failure is on criterion 3: Athena's recorded fmt check failed, and when I reran it rustfmt wanted the new `DIAGNOSE_FAILURE_SKILL` constant in introspect.rs split over two lines. Running `cargo fmt` should fix it. Two minor findings: (1) the skill is in crates/athena-context/skills/ instead of the listed skills/, which is reasonable for include_str! but outside the stated scope; (2) it skips the repository's existing system for versioned, hashed prompts, so a job's record cannot show which version of the method was used.
